title: OpenStax places an understanding of other minds between 3 and 5
summary: OpenStax says that between 3 and 5 years children come to understand that other people have thoughts, feelings, and beliefs different from their own.
body: The lifespan chapter calls that understanding theory of mind. It says children can then tell that someone else holds a false belief, tease, or see why a sibling is angry. The window is 3 to 5 years in this textbook, after the egocentric description of ages 2 to 3. It is a secondary summary of a research tradition, not a pass-fail test and not the CDC milestone list. The chapter cites other authors for the false-belief point; this card uses OpenStax's own summary.

sources.title: OpenStax Psychology

sources.note: Paraphrase only, no quotation. OpenStax Psychology web chapter at /books/psychology/, credited as the first-edition path (CC BY 4.0). Supports the 3-to-5-year statement that children come to understand others' different thoughts, feelings, and beliefs, named theory of mind.
